title: Inquest hears OPP claim that man died of overdose after arrest
article: The inquest into the death of 49-year-old John Roberts began today at the North Bay Courthouse.
Roberts died in hospital on the afternoon of December 15, 2016 while in OPP custody.
Dr. Steven Bodley is presiding as the inquest coroner in front of a five-person jury made up of four women and one man.
Three witnesses are expected to take the stand during the two-day inquest.
This morning, coroner's counsel outlined the summary of what the OPP say occurred on that night, trying to show that Roberts died of a drug overdose.

According to the coroner's counsel, Roberts was pulled over by the OPP after a report came in of an erratic driver weaving into the centre lane of traffic along highway 17. Roberts was eventually pulled over by OPP Sgt. Turner.
In the summary of evidence, when Turner conducted the traffic stop, the Sgt.approached Roberts' vehicle.Roberts then proceeded to get out of the car himself.
Turner was concerned that Roberts appeared to show signs of drug consumption during their conversation and there was also evidence of drug paraphernalia and white powder inside Roberts' vehicle.

According to the summary, Turner then arrested Roberts and charged him with driving while impaired. As they were traveling down the highway, Turner noticed Roberts was having difficulty breathing in the back of the cruiser.Soon after, Turner called another officer and a paramedic to meet him.
When they stopped Roberts appeared to have no vital signs and he was rushed to the North Bay Regional Health Centre where he was pronounced dead around 4:15 p.m.
As part of the investigation into the death, the coroner found significant amounts of Fentanyl and cocaine in his system. The coroner noted Roberts had signs of a previous heart condition.
Roberts mother and daughter were in attendance in the courtroom today.
The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding Mr. Roberts' death throughout the afternoon and into Tuesday.
The jury is expected to make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.
